critique:
refused
  The reported failures all occurred at the initial execution decision, when the goal required reproducing a visible demonstration and no memory had yet been carried in. The policy chose a larger-x clockwise move where the first demonstrated traversal actually went toward smaller x along the upper arc, or chose a clockwise move where the first traversal went toward larger x along the lower arc. None of the reports identified missing information or a missing rule. The complete demonstrations supported routes such as ["D","A","A"], ["C","A","C","C"], ["C","B","D","B"], and ["D","A","C","C","A"], and the annotated memories carried those routes into the subsequent decisions correctly. These failures do not establish a SUFFICIENCY or NECESSITY defect: the current observation supplied the initial traversal, and the existing instructions explicitly map smaller-x upper arcs to D and larger-x lower arcs to C, require selecting the first decoded letter, and forbid substituting a location-based fallback for a supported demonstration move. The later decisions also support the existing one-completed-command, one-leading-letter removal convention. No annotation changes, extra memory fields, or new transition rules are warranted by these reports; the incorrect initial choices are failures to apply rules already present.
